To say that a problem needs a certain number of steps,
we must first fix what a step is.
This page defines the [Turing machine](#def-turing-machine),
the model of computation that complexity theory uses,
and shows why the choice of model hardly matters:
the variants of the model, and ordinary computers,
simulate each other with at most a polynomial increase in
[running time](p-and-np.qmd#def-running-time).
It ends with the universal machine,
one Turing machine that can run every other.
The [asymptotic notation](asymptotic-notation.qmd) page defines the $\asymub{\cdot}$ notation used here.
